title: Remotely-triggerable panic in Taildrop filename dedup (nextFilename slice out of range)
status: CONFIRMED (runtime reproducer run against verbatim function logic; reachability traced in source)
upstream_status: UNFIXED on origin/main as of review (no post-v1.104.1 commits touch feature/taildrop/; tip nextFilename identical)
severity_estimate: Low (contained by net/http per-connection panic recovery: failed transfer + logged panic, not daemon crash)
root_cause: When name matches rxNumberSuffix ` \([0-9]+\)` yet ends with ' (', LastIndex(' (') points at the trailing ' (', so the slice low index (i+2) exceeds the high index (len-1) -> slice bounds out of range panic.
reachability: peerapi PUT /v0/put/<name>; <name> = url.PathUnescape of path tail (feature/taildrop/peerapi.go)
Rename calls nextFilename(filepath.Base(dst)) only on a name COLLISION that is not deduped (different size OR different sha256)
filename passes validateBaseName (taildrop.go:154): verified ACCEPTED for 'x (1) (', 'a (5) (', 'doc (12) ('
caller must hold FileSharingSend cap or be same-user-untagged (canPutFile)
repro: scripts/repro-taildrop-nextfilename/ (go run . -> prints validateBaseName ACCEPTED then PANIC slice bounds out of range [7:6])
attack_sequence: Authorized file-sharing peer: PUT name 'x (1) (' (size A); then PUT same name with size B != A -> Rename sees existing file, sizes differ so sha dedup skipped -> nextFilename('x (1) (') -> panic in the peerapi handler goroutine.
fix: Guard the slice bounds / parse the numeric group via the rxNumberSuffix submatch instead of hand-computed indices.
